title.narrative: Provision of emergency winterization assistance to conflict-affected communities

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ongoing warfare has severely damaged Ukraine's critical energy infrastructure. In the context of ongoing displacement and decreasing economy, many families face rising living costs and income losses, making it difficult to afford heating. The internally displaced people (IDPs) and conflict-affected communities in Ukraine continue to heavily rely on ongoing humanitarian assistance for their survival, whereas the winter conditions further exacerbate the grave humanitarian crisis, straining the already affected communities. People in Need (PIN)'s winterization project aims to provide life-saving assistance to vulnerable populations in Ukraine's frontline oblasts, enhancing resilience and improving living conditions during the harsh winter season. PIN will support vulnerable communities in the five prioritized oblasts – Sumy, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kharkiv, and Mykolaiv – throughout the harsh winter months, complementing ongoing efforts and addressing critical gaps. PIN will provide solid fuel (briquettes) to those most vulnerable, such as people with disabilities (PwD) and the elderly, focusing on newly accessible and isolated frontline areas where market functionality is limited. The project aims to address with these the critical winterization needs for 3,300 households (6,600 individuals, including 2,049 men, nbsp3,369 women, 591 boys and 591 girls), in line with Shelter Cluster Objective 02. This in-kind assistance is deemed most appropriate due to the high vulnerabilities of the target groups, access restrictions, constraints within local markets and community preferences based further on previous needs assessment under PIN´s-UHF current winterization project- CBPF-UKR-23-R-INGO-26176. The intervention aligns with the allocation strategy, HNRP, Winterization Recommendations 2024-2025, Cold Spot assessment, and Shelter Cluster’s East Hub solid fuel monitoring findings. PIN’s capacity to organize direct delivery to beneficiaries' homes ensures efficient and effective assistance, improving living conditions during the cold season. PIN’s proven track record in delivering multi-sectoral support across Ukraine, endorsed by previous UHF grants, supports this project, ensuring its field assessments and lessons learned from previous projects inform this intervention to secure a rapid and effective response. nbsp ltbrgt ltbrgtPIN's approach incorporates gender considerations, disability inclusion, protection mainstreaming, and accountability to the affected population, aligning with UHF's programmatic priorities. Through community work and leveraging on its wide network of CSO partners, PIN has gained a high level of acceptance over the years. Coordination with local authorities, clusters, and humanitarian actors will avoid duplication of resources. Procurement of fuel from accredited local suppliers will revitalize the local market, supporting ethical businesses with strong social commitments. Continuous stakeholder consultations, community feedback mechanisms, and adherence to the Do No Harm principle ensure transparent and impartial assistance. PIN’s comprehensive risk assessment and security protocols in place enhance the safety of staff and operations in high-risk zones. The project also integrates environmental and social responsibility objectives, promoting sustainable practices and improving air quality through the use of high-quality fuel. ltbrgtlt/pgt
